messages:
Alex: Quick sync request — infra + runtime need a minimal rollout metrics spec for the console comparative panels. I sketched the requirements below, want feedback on feasibility and cost tradeoffs.

Maria: thanks — can you list the exact signals you need from runtime vs from infra? helps scope sample rates and retention.

Alex: sure. runtime: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), per-token latency distribution, output token count, early-termination count, kv-cache hit rate, model-variant label, rollout_id. infra: request_count, routed_region, queue_depth, GPU_util, instance_restarts, network_errors. Also need a mergeable "quality" signal from eval infra (see below).

Chris: runtime constraints — collecting full per-token histograms at 100% QPS is heavy. We can expose HDR histograms aggregated per 1m, and approximate per-token with sampled traces (1 in 500). Would that work for the dashboard?

Alex: HDR per-1m bins + sampled token traces seems fine. Console can show approximate token latency bands and a note about sampling. We mainly need comparative deltas between baseline/variant with confidence intervals.

Jamila: on the quality signal — do you mean automated evals (prompt-set) fed into the rollout? or human-labeled quality events?

Alex: both. For A/B panels we want: "quality_lift" (delta in mean score over a sliding window), sample_size, p_value (two-sided), and effect_size (Cohen's d). For production alerts we use a conservative threshold (e.g., p<0.01 AND effect_size > 0.2).

Maria: privacy and sampling note: any payload-level eval must be sampled and sanitized. We should only ship metric tags and numeric scores, never raw prompts or outputs in telemetry. Add an eval_tag label so customers can opt in per rollout.

Chris: proposed Prometheus label model (runtime exporters):
```
rollout_id="r-2026-05-01-01", model="redwood-v1", variant="quantized-8", route="chat_completions", region="us-east-1"
metric examples:
llm_request_count{...} -> counter per variant
llm_latency_histogram_seconds{...} -> HDR buckets per 1m
llm_token_latency_sample{...} -> sampled traces tagged with sample_id
kv_cache_hit_ratio{...} -> gauge per model/instance
quality_score_summary{rollout_id, eval_tag, window="30m"} -> gauge: mean_score
```

Jamila: that looks good. For quality we should also emit sample_size and stddev so console can compute CI if needed.

Alex: agreed. Example JSON push (for the eval pipeline) for comparative row: 
```json
{
  "rollout_id": "r-2026-05-01-01",
  "baseline_variant": "redwood-v1",
  "variant": "redwood-v1-quant8",
  "window_secs": 1800,
  "baseline_mean": 4.12,
  "variant_mean": 3.95,
  "baseline_std": 0.6,
  "variant_std": 0.72,
  "baseline_n": 1250,
  "variant_n": 1208,
  "p_value": 0.007,
  "cohens_d": -0.25
}
```

Chris: runtime can produce that JSON from the sampled evals service and push to the metrics-pipeline. Cost estimate: additional 0.3% CPU for aggregation on high QPS hosts; we can offload heavy math to a separate worker if product wants lower runtime impact.

Maria: who owns the prometheus label contract? We need infra to guarantee these labels are present and stable across deploys, otherwise dashboards break.

SRE-Bot: Created infra ticket INF-2398 to formalize label contract and retention policy (link: https://issues.redwood/INF-2398).

Leo: Console/UX ask: show a compact comparative row per rollout with: baseline_mean, variant_mean, delta%, p_value, effect_size, sample_size, traffic_split. Also include visualized CI band and a sparkline of p99 latency. Can we get sample_size and traffic_split from runtime tags?

Chris: traffic_split is available from the router (we can emit routed_fraction{rollout_id,variant}). Runtime will ensure routed_fraction is exported once per 15s. Sample_size derives from llm_request_count over the window.

Alex: next steps: (1) infra formalizes label contract in INF-2398, (2) runtime implements HDR histograms + sampled token traces + JSON eval summary push, (3) console implements comparative row UI and alerts using p_value/effect_size. I'll add proposed alert thresholds in a follow-up.

Maria: +1, will review INF-2398 and add retention/PII constraints.

Jamila: +1 from eval infra, will add stddev and n to the JSON output.

Chris: ETA for runtime changes: prototype in a branch by EOW, rollout to canary nodes next week.

Alex: perfect — thanks all. If you have blocking perf numbers call them out here, otherwise I'll take this to product for UI mockups. :thumbsup:
